blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Ten inspectors are to cover eight substations, one each at least cost, and at most three of the inspectors may come from the north office. Which OR-Tools tool states this rule directly?

options.text: SimpleLinearSumAssignment, with the north office's costs raised until 3 remain
options.says: Raising costs only discourages north inspectors; it never caps them at three.

options.text: SimpleLinearSumAssignment, padded with dummy substations to hold the north office to 3
options.says: Padding squares the table; it does not limit how many north inspectors get real substations.

options.text: A MIP only, as a cap of 3 on the north office has no form as a flow
options.says: The lesson's team rule was a flow with a node per team, matching the MIP's 250.

options.text: SimpleMinCostFlow, with a north office node capped at 3
options.says: Right: a node per group with a capacity on its incoming arc states the cap, as the teams example did.

origin.section: A Side Rule Moves Assignment to a Min-Cost Flow or a MIP

questions.stem: A program creates KnapsackSolver with KNAPSACK_DYNAMIC_PROGRAMMING_SOLVER and calls init with two weight lists, one for budget and one for crew-months, inside try/except Exception. What happens?

options.text: The except block catches an error, since the type refuses a second row
options.says: No Python exception is raised; the lesson's child processes ended with exit code -6.

options.text: The whole process stops, since the failed check is not a Python exception
options.says: Right: the one-row types stopped the process on two rows, which no except block can catch.

options.text: The solve uses the budget row alone, since the type reads one row
options.says: The run never got to a solve; the process stopped with the check's message.

options.text: The solve uses both rows, since the type accepts any number of rows
options.says: Only the MULTIDIMENSION types returned a value (7513) on two rows.

origin.section: KnapsackSolver Picks Yes/No Items Under Capacity Rows, and Its Type Must Fit the Rows

questions.stem: Jobs adding up to 61 crew-months must be packed whole into 10-month seasons. First fit decreasing uses 7 seasons. What can the planners conclude without a MIP?

options.text: A MIP might still find 6, since first fit decreasing is a heuristic
options.says: 61 months need at least ceil(61/10) = 7 seasons, so 6 is impossible.

options.text: Nothing yet, since only a MIP can prove that a packing is optimal
options.says: A heuristic count equal to the lower bound is proved optimal by the bound alone.

options.text: 7 is the fewest, since it equals 61/10 rounded up, which no packing beats
options.says: Right: the lower bound is 7 and the heuristic reaches it, as in the crew-seasons run.

options.text: 6.1 is the fewest, since the bound is 61/10 and seasons may be shared
options.says: Seasons are whole and each job is done whole, so the bound is rounded up.

origin.section: Bin Packing Minimizes the Number of Bins, and a Lower Bound Can Prove a Heuristic Optimal
